# DIP public site and GitHub workspace

Public landing page and private, read-only GitHub dashboard for dip.vxu.me. Built with React/Vinext on Sites, with D1 holding OAuth state and encrypted, expiring sessions.

## Setup

Create a public GitHub App with Contents: read and Metadata: read. Disable webhooks. Callback: `https://dip.vxu.me/api/github/callback`; setup URL: `https://dip.vxu.me/dashboard`. Keep expiring user tokens enabled. Each user installs the app on their selected repositories and authorizes their own identity.

Set `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_SLUG`, and secret values `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, `DIP_SESSION_KEY` through Sites environment configuration. The session key must be a cryptographically random 32-byte base64url value. Never commit secret values. Production D1 migrations are in `drizzle/`.

## Behavior and boundaries

Discovery scans authorized installation repositories on their default branch for `.dip/events`. A selected project can read another branch. Reads are pinned to a commit and DIP tree until refreshed. Task projection respects causal ancestry and exposes conflicts and missing history. Activity loads in pages; commits link to GitHub diffs. Local, uncommitted data and live lease ownership are not available to the website. Recorded evidence is historical and is never presented as a fresh verification.

OAuth uses PKCE and one-time state tied to a Secure HttpOnly cookie. Session IDs are opaque and hashed in D1; provider tokens are AES-GCM encrypted at rest. Tokens stay server-side. Sessions expire after at most eight hours, with no persisted refresh token. API data is private/no-store, and POST requests require same origin. Repository reads use the requesting user's token; no shared organization token is deployed.

GitHub tree truncation, malformed events, API failures and rate limits are visible. Individual event reads are bounded to 1 MiB, batches to 32 files and approximately 4 MiB, provider responses to 16 Mi
